mainTopic: Apple-juice leavening, the dry מנחת חוטא, and measuring food by its current or original size
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא about leavening the מנחות that are brought as חמץ. The רבנן say apple juice cannot be used, while רבי חנינא בן גמליאל (or רבי חנינא בן תרדיון, according to רב כהנא) says it can. The גמרא shows that a משנה forbidding dough leavened by a mashed apple fits even the רבנן, because the dough still becomes נוקשה, partial leaven. Next, רבי אילא says the dry מנחת חוטא is the hardest מנחה for קמיצה. רב יצחק בר אבדימי says it may be kneaded with water. The גמרא first suggests they argue about measuring a מנחה as it is now or as it was before. It concludes instead that they argue about whether חריבה means dry of oil or dry of everything. The same measuring question then comes up with meat that swelled or shrank in cooking, where two groups of אמוראים disagree. Two ברייתות are brought to challenge the view that the original size counts. The amud ends with רבה's rule: meat that shrinks below the minimum size no longer counts, while meat that grows into it counts only מדרבנן.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says apple juice can leaven
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with the רבנן's rule that you do not leaven with apples. A dissenting opinion in the name of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says you may.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One may not leaven] with apples. In the name of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל they said: one may leaven [with them].
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the previous page finishes: the רבנן say apple juice is not a proper way to leaven these מנחות. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל disagrees and says it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two views here. The רבנן hold that apple juice does not produce real leavening. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל holds that it does, so a מנחה leavened this way counts as leavened.

keyTerms.meaning: We leaven, meaning we make the dough rise and become חמץ
Apples (here, apple juice used to make dough rise)
In the name of

phrases.english: with apples.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: the רבנן said you may not leaven these offerings with apples.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel they said:
One may leaven [with them].

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from the previous amud and adds the dissenting view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן say apple juice does not leaven. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says it does.

steps.title: רב כהנא gives a different name for the dissenting opinion
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא taught the same opinion in the name of רבי חנינא בן תרדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא would teach it in the name of רבי חנינא בן תרדיון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes a different tradition about who said the lenient opinion. רב כהנא says it was רבי חנינא בן תרדיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the name changes here, not the הלכה. The ruling that apple juice can leaven stays the same. It is just credited to a different sage with a similar first name.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana would teach it
in the name of Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another tradition for who said the opinion in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lenient opinion is credited to רבי חנינא בן תרדיון instead of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Whose view matches the משנה about a mashed apple in dough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if a mashed apple was put into dough and leavened it, the dough is forbidden. It asks whose opinion this follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: In accordance with whom is that which we learned: An apple that one mashed and placed into dough, and it leavened it, this [dough] is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that treats an apple as something that leavens dough. It asks which side of the argument this matches. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes the apple really did leaven the dough, and that is why the dough becomes forbidden. That sounds like the view that apple juice leavens. So it seems to go against the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with whose view does it go?
He mashed or crushed it
Dough
It leavened it (made the dough rise)

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which we learned:
An apple that one mashed
phrases.notes: This משנה is in תרומות. It is talking about a תרומה apple mixed into ordinary dough.

phrases.english: and placed it into the dough,
and it leavened it — this [dough] is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the argument in step 1 against another משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion about apple leavening does the משנה in תרומות follow?

steps.title: Suggestion: the משנה follows only רבי חנינא בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה follows רבי חנינא בן גמליאל and not the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like whom? Shall we say it is רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, and not the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that the משנה only works for רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, who says apples really leaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this were true, the משנה would go against the רבנן, who are the majority view. Having a משנה follow only a minority view is a problem, so the גמרא will try to avoid this.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
The Rabbis, the majority opinion

phrases.english: Like whom?

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא,
phrases.english: Shall we say it is Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel,
and not the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא וְלָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the רבנן that apple juice does not leaven
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids dough because an apple leavened it. That seems to assume apples truly leaven, which the רבנן deny.

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree: it becomes partial leaven
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can follow the רבנן too. Apple-leavened dough is not full חמץ, but it is at least נוקשה, partly leavened.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it is the רבנן. Granted that it is not full חמץ, it is at least hardened [partial] leaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Even the רבנן agree the apple has some leavening effect, enough to make the dough נוקשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן only said apple juice does not make full חמץ, so it is not good enough to leaven a מנחה. But it still makes partial leaven. That is enough to say the apple affected the dough, and so the dough is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (the answer works even for the other view)
Granted that
Full, complete leaven
Hardened leaven: dough that has only partly leavened

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן say apple juice makes only נוקשה (partial leaven), not full חמץ. So the משנה forbidding apple-leavened dough fits everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן do not say apple juice has no effect at all. They only say it does not make full חמץ.

phrases.english: You can even say it is the Rabbis;
granted that it is not full chametz,
it is at least hardened [partial] leaven.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the opinion: the רבנן deny only full leavening, not partial leavening
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן hold that apple juice has no leavening effect, so the משנה must follow רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן agree that apple juice makes נוקשה, so the משנה fits their view too.

steps.title: רבי אילא: the מנחת חוטא is the hardest to take a handful from
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילא says no מנחה is harder to do קמיצה on than the מנחת חוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא said: You have no greater difficulty for taking a handful than the מנחת חוטא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי אילא says taking a handful from the מנחת חוטא is harder than from any other מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחת חוטא is brought without oil, so the flour is dry and loose. When the כהן scoops it, flour easily slips out, so getting an exact handful is hard.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן taking a handful of the מנחה to burn on the מזבח
The meal offering of a sinner, brought without oil or frankincense
Difficulty

phrases.english: Rabbi Ila said:
You have no greater difficulty for taking a handful
than the sinner's meal offering.
phrases.notes: He means it is hard because this מנחה has no oil, so the dry flour slips out of the hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא אֵין לְךָ הַקָּשָׁה לִקְמִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about קמיצה, unrelated to apple leavening
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dry מנחת חוטא is the hardest מנחה for קמיצה.

steps.title: רב יצחק בר אבדימי: knead it with water
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבדימי says the מנחת חוטא may be kneaded with water and stays valid, so it is not especially hard to take a handful from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אבדימי said: The מנחת חוטא — he kneads it with water, and it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר אבדימי disagrees with רבי אילא. The כהן can knead the מנחת חוטא with water, so the flour holds together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids oil in a מנחת חוטא, but water is not forbidden. Water makes the flour stick together, so the קמיצה is no harder than for other מנחות.

keyTerms.meaning: He kneads it (mixes the flour with liquid)
Valid, fit to be offered

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the ban on oil in a מנחת חוטא does not ban every liquid. Water is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi said:
The sinner's meal offering — he kneads it with water,
and it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי אָמַר מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא מְגַבְּלָהּ בַּמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אילא's claim in step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that קמיצה of the מנחת חוטא is especially difficult
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אילא assumed the flour must stay completely dry, but it may be kneaded with water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחת חוטא may be kneaded with water and remains valid, so its קמיצה is not especially hard.

steps.title: Maybe the dispute is about measuring the flour now or as it was before
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי אילא and רב יצחק בר אבדימי disagree about whether a מנחה is measured as it is now or as it was before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is what they argue about. One Sage holds that we measure the מנחה as it is now. The other Sage holds that we measure it as it was before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a guess about the real root of the argument between רבי אילא and רב יצחק בר אבדימי from the last two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we measure the dough as it is now, adding water causes no problem, so the קמיצה is not hard (רב יצחק בר אבדימי). If we measure it as it was when it was dry flour, the water makes it hard to know how much flour is in the handful. That would make the מנחת חוטא especially hard to do קמיצה on (רבי אילא).

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say; the גמרא is offering a suggestion
They disagree
We measure
As they are now
As they were before

phrases.english: Let us say that they disagree about this:
one Sage holds: we measure them as they are,
phrases.notes: This is רב יצחק בר אבדימי's side: measure the dough as it is now, after the water.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: we measure them as they were.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the underlying reason behind the dispute between steps 6 and 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What basic principle are רבי אילא and רב יצחק בר אבדימי arguing about?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggestion: they argue about whether we measure a מנחה by its current or its original size. Step 9 rejects this.

steps.title: No: everyone measures as it is now; they argue about what "dry" means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone agrees we measure as it is now. The argument is whether חריבה means dry of oil only or dry of everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that we measure them as they are now. This is what they argue about. One Sage holds that "dry" means dry of oil. The other Sage holds that it means dry of everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away its own guess and gives a different reason for the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measuring principle is now the same for both sides. The argument moves to the meaning of the word חריבה ("dry") in the פסוק. רב יצחק בר אבדימי says it only means no oil, so water is fine. רבי אילא says it means nothing at all, not even water, which is why the dough is hard to handle.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Dry; the word the פסוק uses for some מנחות
Oil
From anything at all

phrases.english: No, for everyone agrees
that we measure them as they are,
and this is what they disagree about:
one Sage holds: what does "dry" mean?
dry of oil,
and the other Sage holds: dry of everything.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּמוֹת שֶׁהֵן מְשַׁעֲרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 8 and puts a different explanation in its place.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the dispute is about the measuring principle.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sides can agree we measure as it is now. The dispute can be explained instead by how each reads the word חריבה.
steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: both sides measure the מנחה as it is now. רב יצחק בר אבדימי reads חריבה as dry of oil only, so water is allowed. רבי אילא reads it as dry of everything, so even water is not allowed.

steps.title: A משנה about meat that swelled or shrank in cooking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: calf meat that swelled and meat of an old animal that shrank are measured "לכמות שהן".
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: meat of a calf that swelled, and meat of an old animal that shrank, are measured according to what they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source where the same measuring question comes up, now about meat. It is setting up the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking changes the size of meat. A calf's meat grows and an old animal's meat shrinks. This matters when we need to know if a piece reaches a required size. The משנה's words "לכמות שהן" are unclear: do they mean the size now, or the size before cooking?

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of a calf
Swelled, grew bigger
Meat of an old animal
Shrank, got squeezed smaller
They are measured

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" is a משנה in מסכת עוקצין.

phrases.english: meat of a calf that swelled,
and meat of an old animal that shrank,
are measured according to what they are.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the idea from step 8, measuring as it is now versus as it was, and shows it in another area of הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat that swelled or shrank in cooking is measured "לכמות שהן". The exact meaning is left for the next step.

steps.title: אמוראים disagree: measure the meat as it is now, or as it was
steps.stepSummary: רב, רבי חייא and רבי יוחנן say the meat is measured as it is now. שמואל, רבי שמעון בר רבי and ריש לקיש say it is measured according to its original size.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב, רבי חייא and רבי יוחנן say: they are measured as they are now. שמואל, רבי שמעון בר רבי and ריש לקיש say: they are measured according to what they were.
steps.whatsHappening: Two groups of אמוראים argue about how to read the משנה's words about measuring the cooked meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first group measures the meat in its current, cooked size. The second group measures it by its size before cooking. So a calf's piece that only reached the needed size by swelling would not count for the second group. An old animal's piece that shrank below the size would still count.

keyTerms.meaning: As they are now, after the change
Here: according to what they originally were

steps.confusionAlert: The two opinions sound almost the same: כמות שהן and לכמות שהן. The extra ל is the whole difference. The second group reads it as "according to their original size," not their size now.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the question from step 8, measuring by current or original size, is a real dispute in other parts of הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: רַב וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rav, Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Yochanan say:
they are measured as they are now,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוּאֵל וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Shmuel, Rabbi Shimon bar Rabbi and Reish Lakish say:
they are measured according to what they were.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the unclear wording of the משנה quoted in step 10 in two different ways.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One group measures cooked meat by its current size. The other group measures it by its original size.

steps.title: A teaching about swollen calf meat challenges the original-size view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that calf meat which swelled to the minimum size can become impure from then on. This suggests we measure by current size, against שמואל and those with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Calf meat that did not have the minimum size, and then swelled until it reached the minimum size, is pure for the past but impure from now on!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the opinion of שמואל, רבי שמעון בר רבי and ריש לקיש from step 11, using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food needs a minimum size to become impure. The ברייתא says meat that was too small, and then swelled, counts as impure from now on. That means its current size counts, which goes against the view that we measure by original size.

keyTerms.meaning: The minimum required size (for food טומאה, the size of an egg)
Swelled, grew bigger
For the past, for what happened before
From now on

steps.confusionAlert: 'Pure for the past' does not mean the meat was pure and then went bad. It means that earlier contact with טומאה, when it was too small, does not count. From now on, at its new size, it can become impure.

phrases.english: They challenged: meat of a calf
that did not have the minimum size,
phrases.notes: For food to become impure it needs to be at least the size of an egg.

phrases.english: and it swelled and reached the minimum size –
it is pure regarding the past,
and impure from here on!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second opinion in step 11 (original size).
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל, רבי שמעון בר רבי and ריש לקיש, who measure by original size
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats swollen meat as impure because of its new size, so the current size is what counts.

steps.title: The impurity of the swollen meat is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that by תורה law the meat goes by its original size. The ברייתא's ruling that it is impure from now on is only a rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל and those with him in one word: the ברייתא is talking about a rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תורה law, the meat is measured by its original small size, so it cannot become impure. The חכמים added a stricter rule that treats it as impure because of its new size. So the ברייתא does not prove what the תורה law is.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not by Torah law

phrases.english: It is by rabbinic law.
phrases.notes: Meaning: by Torah law the original size counts, but the חכמים were strict.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows the Torah law measures by current size.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only a rabbinic stringency; by Torah law the original size counts.

steps.title: The end of the teaching mentions פיגול and נותר, which are תורה laws
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying the same applies to פיגול and נותר. These are תורה laws, so how can the ברייתא be talking only about rabbinic law?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the ברייתא: 'And the same applies to פיגול, and the same applies to נותר.' It makes sense if you say the ברייתא is תורה law, since פיגול and נותר exist. But if you say it is rabbinic law, are there פיגול and נותר by rabbinic law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 13 by quoting the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול and נותר are prohibitions from the תורה. If the ברייתא were only about rabbinic rules, it would make no sense to say 'the same applies' to תורה prohibitions. So the ברייתא seems to be about תורה law after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a משנה or ברייתא
A קרבן brought with the plan to eat it after its allowed time; forbidden by the Torah
Meat of a קרבן left over after its time to eat it ran out
By Torah law
It makes sense / granted (used to show one option works and the other does not)

phrases.english: If so, say the last part:
And the same with פיגול, and the same with נותר.
It makes sense if you say it is Torah law,
that is why there are פיגול and נותר,
but if you say it is rabbinic law,
is there פיגול and נותר by rabbinic law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rabbinic-law answer of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is only rabbinic
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the ברייתא compares to פיגול and נותר, which are Torah laws, so the whole ברייתא seems to be Torah law.

steps.title: The teaching means the rabbinic impurity of פיגול and נותר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the end of the ברייתא as talking about the טומאה that the חכמים put on פיגול and נותר, which is rabbinic. So the whole ברייתא can be rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: 'And the same with the טומאה of פיגול, and the same with the טומאה of נותר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 14 by reading the end of the ברייתא in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not talking about the תורה prohibition of eating פיגול and נותר. It is talking about the טומאה the חכמים gave them, which is rabbinic. So the whole ברייתא stays rabbinic, and שמואל's view that the תורה law goes by original size still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The impurity the חכמים attached to פיגול meat
The impurity the חכמים attached to נותר meat

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about swollen calf meat does not disprove שמואל, רבי שמעון בר רבי and ריש לקיש. It is all rabbinic, including its end, which is about the rabbinic טומאה of פיגול and נותר.

phrases.english: Say: and the same with the impurity of פיגול,
phrases.notes: The חכמים made פיגול and נותר cause impurity even when the meat itself is not impure. That rule is rabbinic.

phrases.english: and the same with the impurity of נותר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 and saves the answer of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The end of the ברייתא refers to the Torah prohibitions of פיגול and נותר.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers to the rabbinic טומאה of פיגול and נותר, so the whole ברייתא is rabbinic.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא needed to mention פיגול and נותר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ending of the ברייתא was needed. Without it, we might think the חכמים would not be this strict about a טומאה that is itself only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since the impurity of פיגול and נותר is only rabbinic, the רבנן would not be this strict in a rabbinic matter. So the ברייתא teaches us that they were.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא bothered to say 'the same applies to פיגול and נותר.' This finishes the answer from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 we learned that the ending of the ברייתא is about the rabbinic טומאה of פיגול and נותר. That raises a question: why say it at all? The answer is that we might have thought the חכמים would not stack one stringency (counting swelled meat) on top of a טומאה that is already only rabbinic. The ברייתא teaches that they did.

keyTerms.meaning: It might have entered your mind to say (the mistaken first thought)
It teaches us (the point the text is making)
This much; to such an extent
The impurity the חכמים put on פיגול and נותר meat

phrases.english: It might have entered your mind to say:
Since the impurity of פיגול
and the impurity of נותר are rabbinic,
this much, in a rabbinic matter,
phrases.notes: He means being strict about meat that only reached the minimum size after swelling.

phrases.english: the Rabbis did not do.
So it teaches us [that they did].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of step 15 by explaining why the ברייתא's ending is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why a seemingly unneeded clause is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים would not be strict about swelled meat when the טומאה itself is only rabbinic.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even for the rabbinic טומאה of פיגול and נותר, swelled meat that reaches the minimum size counts.

steps.title: A ברייתא about old meat that shrank
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says impure old-animal meat that shrank below the minimum size made things impure in the past, but is pure from now on. This seems to show we measure by current size, against שמואל and those with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: meat of an old animal that was the minimum size and then shrank below it is impure for the past and pure from now on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא, this time about meat that got smaller instead of bigger. It seems to go by the meat's current size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the ברייתא was about calf meat that swelled. Now it is old-animal meat that shrank. If the meat no longer passes on טומאה once it shrank, it seems we look at its present size. That challenges שמואל, רבי שמעון בר רבי and ריש לקיש, who say we measure by the original size.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of an old animal, which shrinks when cooked
Shrank
The minimum size needed for the law to apply
For the past
From now on

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Meat of an old animal that was the minimum size,
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of the calf meat in step 12: old meat shrinks when cooked instead of swelling.

phrases.english: and it shrank to less than the minimum size,
is impure for the past,
phrases.notes: Things it touched while it was still big enough became impure.

phrases.english: and pure from now on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on the dispute of step 11, this time about shrinking meat.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל, רבי שמעון בר רבי and ריש לקיש, who measure by the original size
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If original size decided, the shrunken meat would still pass on טומאה. The ברייתא says it is pure from now on, so current size decides.

steps.title: רבה's rule for shrinking and growing
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that when something shrinks below the minimum size, it simply no longer has the size. When something grows into the minimum size, it counts only by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: whenever something first had the minimum size and now does not, it simply does not have it. Whenever something first did not have the minimum size and now does, it counts only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives one rule that explains both ברייתות. Shrinking and growing are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shrinking: once the meat is too small, it is too small, and its original size does not help. That matches the second ברייתא. Growing: by תורה law the new size does not count, and the meat counts only מדרבנן. That matches the answer in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: At first; originally
Now
It does not have [the minimum size]
By rabbinic law, not Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: Meat that shrinks below the minimum size stops passing on טומאה from now on. Meat that swells into the minimum size counts only by rabbinic law.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying we always follow the current size. For meat that grew, תורה law still looks at the original small size, and only the חכמים made it count.

phrases.english: רבה said:
Any case where at first it had [the minimum size],
and now it does not have it,
it simply does not have it.
phrases.notes: So we look at the size it is now; its bigger past size doesn't help.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא לָא הֲוָה בֵּיהּ
phrases.english: And any case where at first it did not have it,
and now it does have it,
it counts by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by separating shrinking from growing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות together seem to prove that current size always decides.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shrinking below the minimum size always counts as too small. Growing into the minimum size counts only by rabbinic law.
